episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: Questions & Answers
episodes.description: Join us for an engaging Q&A session with esteemed scholars Dr. Giszczak and Dr. Michael Barber as they tackle a range of fascinating questions about the Bible. Our experts delve into essential books that every Catholic should know beyond the Gospels and New Testament letters, highlighting the foundational significance of Genesis and the Psalms. We also explore the remarkable discoveries of the Dead Sea Scrolls, their impact on biblical studies, and the significance of texts like the Book of Tobit. Additionally, we address what Simeon meant by saying Mary's heart would be pierced, the events du

episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: Jesus and the Mystery of the Beatitudes
episodes.short: Anchored Bible Conference: Jesus and the Mystery of the Beatitudes
episodes.description: This episode addresses common misconceptions about the Beatitudes and provides practical insights on how to live them out in our daily lives. Whether you're facing challenges, seeking spiritual growth, or simply looking to deepen your faith, this episode offers valuable guidance and inspiration.

episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: The Quest for Wisdom and Co-Reigning with Christ
episodes.short: Anchored Bible Conference: The Quest for Wisdom and Co-Reigning with Christ
episodes.description: In this enlightening episode, Dr. Mark Giszczak, Associate Professor of Sacred Scripture at the Augustine Institute, shares his profound insights on the quest for wisdom as depicted in the Bible. Dr. Giszczak explores the intricate connections between wisdom and kingship, highlighting how the desire for wisdom leads to a kingdom, drawing from his expertise in Old Testament wisdom literature. Using the Wisdom of Solomon as a focal point, he explains the significance of wisdom in both ancient and contemporary contexts, illustrating how wisdom is the ultimate intellectual virtue that guides us to

episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: Finding Consolation in the Book of Revelation
episodes.short: Anchored Bible Conference: Finding Consolation in the Book of Revelation
episodes.description: In this episode, we explore the often misunderstood Book of Revelation, revealing its message of hope and consolation during times of persecution and suffering. Drawing insights from the commentary of German New Testament scholar and Bishop Edward Schick, we uncover a Catholic perspective that provides powerful insights into the present state of the church and the world.

episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: Jesus and the Jewish Roots of Mary
episodes.short: Anchored Bible Conference: Jesus and the Jewish Roots of Mary
episodes.description: Join Dr. Brandt Pitre as he presents insights from his latest book, Jesus and the Jewish Roots of Mary, focusing on the unique typology of Mary as the new Rachel. In light of the turmoil in today's world, Dr. Pitre explores the profound connections between Mary and Rachel, revealing Mary's role as the mother of the new Israel. Discover how understanding the Jewish roots of Mary enriches our perception of her identity and mission, as Dr. Pitre delves into scriptural parallels and ancient traditions that highlight Mary's intercessory power and maternal care.

episodes.title: Anchored Bible Conference: Unshakable Hope
episodes.description: In this episode, we delve into the profound message of unshakable hope found in the Epistle to the Hebrews. Join us as we explore how the promises of God serve as an anchor for our souls, providing stability and security amidst life's storms. Through an in-depth study of Hebrews chapter six and other key passages, we uncover the significance of God's promises to Abraham and David, and how these promises are fulfilled in Jesus Christ. Discover how faith and hope are intertwined, and how the assurance of God's character and His promises can strengthen us to persevere with patient endurance. Whet

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Question and Answer
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Question and Answer
episodes.description: Dr. Pitre takes time to answer numerous questions regarding the material covered over the course of the study.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Resurrection of Jesus
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Resurrection of Jesus
episodes.description: What is the Resurrection? What do we mean when we say Jesus “rose from the dead”? Dr. Pitre lays out the evidence for the Resurrection of Jesus, focusing on three things:the empty tomb, the appearances of Jesus to his disciples, and the fulfillment of scripture.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Crucifixion of Jesus
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Crucifixion of Jesus
episodes.description: Why would Jesus, who preached about the love of God, detachment form worldly goods, and love of one’s neighbor, be so violently opposed that his enemies arranged his execution? In this session, Dr. Pitre looks at the details surrounding Jesus’s trial and Death and what these details reveal about Jesus and his mission.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Did Jesus Claim to Be God?
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Did Jesus Claim to Be God?
episodes.description: What answers can we give skeptics who think that the early Christians exaggerated stories about Jesus and made him out to be something he was not? Dr. Pitre takes an in-depth look at three particular New Testament passages that show Jesus’s revelation of his divinity and his disciples’ understanding that Jesus is the one true God.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Kingdom of God and the Messiah
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Kingdom of God and the Messiah
episodes.description: Who did Jesus claim to be? Who was he? Looking at Jesus’s own words and his fulfillment of two key Old Testament prophecies in the Book of Daniel, Dr. Pitre opens up Jesus’s oft repeated promise to usher in the Kingdom of God.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: When Were the Gospels Written?
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: When Were the Gospels Written?
episodes.description: Some attempt to cast doubt on the reliability of the Gospels, asserting they were written too late in the first century to provide accurate information about Jesus. Is there any evidence that the Gospels were written closer to the events they describe? And how did the disciples’ training as students influence the reliability of their witness?

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Are the Gospels Biographies?
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Are the Gospels Biographies?
episodes.description: Do the Gospels tell us the truth about Jesus? Or should we view them as folklore, fables, or legends? Dr. Pitre demonstrates how the Gospels are best understood as ancient biographies, and, consequently, as reliable sources of historical information about Jesus.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Early Church Fathers
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: The Early Church Fathers
episodes.description: The early church is not silent on the authorship of the Gospels. From the earliest members of the Christian faith, the early Church Fathers, we learn how well-attested it was that the Gospels are in fact written by Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.

episodes.title: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Were the Gospels Anonymous?
episodes.short: Lectio The Case for Jesus: Were the Gospels Anonymous?
episodes.description: Can we trust the Gospels? Were these accounts written by individuals with firsthand knowledge of Jesus Christ? Dr. Brant Pitre begins this series by examining why the Gospels are reliable sources of information about Jesus and by looking at the historical evidence that backs up this claim.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Question and Answer
episodes.description: As the study comes to the end, we pause to reflect on some questions that have arisen during our journey through Mark's Gospel.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Jesus's Suffering, Death and Resurrection
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Jesus's Suffering, Death and Resurrection
episodes.description: Those mocking Jesus at the foot of the Cross are silenced when he utters a single sentence. As Jesus breathes his last and the Temple veil is torn, Mark records the words uttered by the Roman centurion, words which signal that God's people will finally see, hear and understand.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Servant of the Lord
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Servant of the Lord
episodes.description: In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus's hour finally arrives—the hour of betrayal and suffering, but also the hour of salvation and glory. Christ the King will be falsely accused, mocked, and tortured, but he will ascend the throne of the Cross and draw the whole world into his reign of love.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Signs of the End
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Signs of the End
episodes.description: The Temple in Jerusalem was God's glorious dwelling with his chosen people, but it was only a house made by human hands. Jesus proclaims a new Temple, not made with hands, that surpasses the stone building in Jerusalem. Jesus gives himself to us and to dwell in our hearts, anticipating the day that we will dwell with him in Heaven.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Jesus and the Temple
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Jesus and the Temple
episodes.description: As the final week before his Passion begins, Jesus has stern warnings for those who would oppose God by rejecting his beloved Son. Will we also reject his words, or will we heed the call to be faithful by rendering unto God the things that are God's?

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Way of Discipleship
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Way of Discipleship
episodes.description: As Jesus makes his way to Jerusalem, three times he predicts his approaching Passion. In response to the disciples' rejection of his words, Jesus works to heal their understanding both of his kingship and of the true nature of Christian discipleship.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Mystery of the Bread
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Mystery of the Bread
episodes.description: The mystery of the bread, the Eucharistic Presence of God, begins to be revealed in the miraculous multiplication of the loaves and fishes. Jesus reveals himself as the divine giver of a new manna. Yet, as Isaiah foretold, the disciples struggle to understand the significance of his deeds.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Faith Not Fear
episodes.description: In the midst of a great storm the disciples cry out in fear. Jesus's words to his frightened disciples are also a challenge to us. In the storms of our life, will we focus on the wind and waves and give in to fear, or will we keep our eyes firmly fixed on Christ in faith?

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Parable of the Sower
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Parable of the Sower
episodes.description: The voice of the Lord calls the cosmos into existence and shakes all creation with its power. Jesus, the Incarnate Word of God, speaks with the same power and authority. But we must have ears to hear if his word is to bear fruit in our lives.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Binding the Strong Man
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Binding the Strong Man
episodes.description: Jesus's appointing of the Twelve Apostles and his many mighty signs show him as the mighty savior who rescues us from the snares of the devil and from sin, saving us from oppression and for the intimate relationship of discipleship.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Feasting and Fasting
episodes.description: When Jesus says to the paralytic, "Your sins are forgiven," the scribes and Pharisees are taken aback and question, "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" Who is this Jesus who has come to earth with heavenly authority, not just to heal temporal ills but for much more. As his mission unfolds, opposition mounts and the scribes and Pharisees attempt to sow discord between Jesus and his disciples.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Come, Follow Behind Me
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Come, Follow Behind Me
episodes.description: Following his baptism in the Jordan River and temptation in the wilderness, Jesus returns to Galilee where he invites the first disciples to follow behind him, and begins the work of regathering the scattered people of God.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Prepare the Way of the Lord
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Prepare the Way of the Lord
episodes.description: The opening lines of Mark's Gospel proclaim that Jesus is, without a doubt, the Son of God. He is the one for whom the way is being prepared. As Jesus sets out on that way, fulfilling the Old Testament _prophecies and prefigurements, Mark shows the Son doing precisely the work of the Father.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Saint Mark the Evangelist
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Saint Mark the Evangelist
episodes.description: Just who is St. Mark, the author of this short but action-packed Gospel? Using outside sources, other books of the Bible, and the Gospel itself, Dr. Gray takes a closeup look at St. Mark, and his connection with St. Peter and the Christians of Rome.

episodes.description: Do you desire to grow in your understanding and devotion to the Luminous Mysteries of the Rosary? episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Question and Answer
episodes.description: As the study comes to the end, we pause to reflect on some questions that have arisen during our journey through Mark's Gospel.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Jesus's Suffering, Death and Resurrection
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Jesus's Suffering, Death and Resurrection
episodes.description: Those mocking Jesus at the foot of the Cross are silenced when he utters a single sentence. As Jesus breathes his last and the Temple veil is torn, Mark records the words uttered by the Roman centurion, words which signal that God's people will finally see, hear and understand.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Servant of the Lord
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Servant of the Lord
episodes.description: In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus's hour finally arrives—the hour of betrayal and suffering, but also the hour of salvation and glory. Christ the King will be falsely accused, mocked, and tortured, but he will ascend the throne of the Cross and draw the whole world into his reign of love.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Signs of the End
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Signs of the End
episodes.description: The Temple in Jerusalem was God's glorious dwelling with his chosen people, but it was only a house made by human hands. Jesus proclaims a new Temple, not made with hands, that surpasses the stone building in Jerusalem. Jesus gives himself to us and to dwell in our hearts, anticipating the day that we will dwell with him in Heaven.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Jesus and the Temple
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Jesus and the Temple
episodes.description: As the final week before his Passion begins, Jesus has stern warnings for those who would oppose God by rejecting his beloved Son. Will we also reject his words, or will we heed the call to be faithful by rendering unto God the things that are God's?

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Way of Discipleship
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Way of Discipleship
episodes.description: As Jesus makes his way to Jerusalem, three times he predicts his approaching Passion. In response to the disciples' rejection of his words, Jesus works to heal their understanding both of his kingship and of the true nature of Christian discipleship.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Mystery of the Bread
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Mystery of the Bread
episodes.description: The mystery of the bread, the Eucharistic Presence of God, begins to be revealed in the miraculous multiplication of the loaves and fishes. Jesus reveals himself as the divine giver of a new manna. Yet, as Isaiah foretold, the disciples struggle to understand the significance of his deeds.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Faith Not Fear
episodes.description: In the midst of a great storm the disciples cry out in fear. Jesus's words to his frightened disciples are also a challenge to us. In the storms of our life, will we focus on the wind and waves and give in to fear, or will we keep our eyes firmly fixed on Christ in faith?

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: The Parable of the Sower
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: The Parable of the Sower
episodes.description: The voice of the Lord calls the cosmos into existence and shakes all creation with its power. Jesus, the Incarnate Word of God, speaks with the same power and authority. But we must have ears to hear if his word is to bear fruit in our lives.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Binding the Strong Man
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Binding the Strong Man
episodes.description: Jesus's appointing of the Twelve Apostles and his many mighty signs show him as the mighty savior who rescues us from the snares of the devil and from sin, saving us from oppression and for the intimate relationship of discipleship.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Feasting and Fasting
episodes.description: When Jesus says to the paralytic, "Your sins are forgiven," the scribes and Pharisees are taken aback and question, "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" Who is this Jesus who has come to earth with heavenly authority, not just to heal temporal ills but for much more. As his mission unfolds, opposition mounts and the scribes and Pharisees attempt to sow discord between Jesus and his disciples.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Come, Follow Behind Me
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Come, Follow Behind Me
episodes.description: Following his baptism in the Jordan River and temptation in the wilderness, Jesus returns to Galilee where he invites the first disciples to follow behind him, and begins the work of regathering the scattered people of God.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Prepare the Way of the Lord
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Prepare the Way of the Lord
episodes.description: The opening lines of Mark's Gospel proclaim that Jesus is, without a doubt, the Son of God. He is the one for whom the way is being prepared. As Jesus sets out on that way, fulfilling the Old Testament _prophecies and prefigurements, Mark shows the Son doing precisely the work of the Father.

episodes.title: Lectio Mark: Saint Mark the Evangelist
episodes.short: Lectio Mark: Saint Mark the Evangelist
episodes.description: Just who is St. Mark, the author of this short but action-packed Gospel? Using outside sources, other books of the Bible, and the Gospel itself, Dr. Gray takes a closeup look at St. Mark, and his connection with St. Peter and the Christians of Rome.
